title: Projection-induced completed coefficient pullback and its normalized quotient tower
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], schemes $X,Y$ and a morphism $f:X\to Y$. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $B_X,B_Y$, the projection-induced ring map $B_Y\to f_*B_X$, and ordinary module direct image $f_*$ with this scalar action [def-sf-projection-coefficient-direct-image]. In the categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define $f^*=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}(-)$ as the left adjoint IntegralAmbient.pull of that direct image, with its specified adjunction IntegralAmbient.adjunction. Its additive termwise extension to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is pullComplex. For a module $M$, a pro-etale object $V\to Y$ and $x\in M(V)$, define pullSection by the adjunction unit $M\to f_*f^*M$ on $x$. Let $A_{W,n}$ denote the finite coefficient sheaf at exponent $n+1$, $n\geq0$, with projection $\pi_n:B_W\to A_{W,n}$. Define pullTower on a complex $P$ as the actual reduction tower $((f^*P)\otimes_{B_X}A_{X,n})_n$ with its quotient augmentation and transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $V_f(P)$ be the finite pulled reduction tower [def-a1-integral-finite-pullback-tower]. Define pullTowerIso to be the unique natural strict tower isomorphism $\operatorname{pullTower}\cong V_f$ characterized in every degree, on every base-changed object and for every finite scalar $a$ and section $x$ by $(\operatorname{pullSection}(x))\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes(x\otimes1)$ (finitePullSection); equivalently $(r\otimes x)\otimes a\mapsto\pi_n(r)a\otimes(x\otimes1)$. The existence-and-uniqueness specification is pullTowerModel. Define pullOperationUnit on $P$ as the canonical quotient Roos unit of $f^*P$ followed by the strict Roos functor [def-sf-strict-roos-functor] applied to pullTowerIso. Its product coordinate is the quotient augmentation followed by pullTowerIso and its shifted coordinate is zero. All strict transitions, differentials and chain maps are retained. There is no boundedness, flatness, completeness, constructibility or invertibility hypothesis and no relation between scheme and coefficient universes.
